profiles.meeting_scenario: A planning meeting for a university-hospital collaboration that is preparing a 6-week pilot to apply BCT taxonomy v1 to an existing patient-facing medication-adherence program. The team wants to create a practical coding workflow, a staff training package, and a short summary of findings that can be shared with partner sites in the UK, Canada, and Singapore. The agenda is to decide what the pilot will include, what the training and coding deliverables are, who owns each workstream, and what timeline they are working toward before the next international consortium check-in. The expected outcome is an agreed plan for pilot setup, coder preparation, intervention materials to be reviewed, and a 'ready by July 15' milestone.

members.name: Dr. Nina Patel
members.expertise: Behavior change intervention design, BCT taxonomy coding, pragmatic trial setup
members.background: Nina is a public health researcher who has led several multi-site behavior change projects and previously trained doctoral students to code intervention materials using BCT taxonomy v1 in research settings.
members.private_state: She wants the pilot to be credible enough for a future methods paper, minimize rework before the consortium review, and avoid committing her small research team to producing operational training assets beyond what is needed for the study.
hidden_assumptions: When people say 'the pilot materials,' they mean the core intervention specification documents and scripted patient communications, not all local implementation artifacts.
A training package for BCT coding means a concise researcher-oriented orientation with examples and a calibration exercise, not a scalable onboarding module for new staff.

If the team says the pilot is 'ready by July 15,' that means the coding framework, sampled materials, and initial coder agreement are in place for internal review, even if full coding is still underway.
The 'international sites' are the three partner institutions that already attend the consortium calls, so any examples or terminology can be lightly adapted rather than fully localized.

members.name: Alex Romero
members.expertise: Program rollout planning, staff training operations, clinical workflow documentation
members.background: Alex manages implementation of digital care programs across hospital and community settings and often translates research frameworks into playbooks for nurses, pharmacists, and support staff.
members.private_state: He wants a pilot plan that can be reused for operational rollout, reduce ambiguity for frontline teams, and show leadership that the collaboration will produce something deployable across sites rather than only a research exercise.
hidden_assumptions: When people say 'the pilot materials,' they mean everything a site uses in practice: app prompts, call-center scripts, clinician cheat sheets, escalation emails, and onboarding instructions.
A training package means a reusable staff-facing module with slides, examples, facilitator notes, and a sign-off step so future sites can run it without Nina's team present.
If the team says the pilot is 'ready by July 15,' that means all materials are finalized enough that site leads could begin local preparation immediately after the consortium meeting.

The 'international sites' include the broader hospital network contacts in each country, so examples should already account for local terminology, medication refill pathways, and regional communication norms.

misalignment_points.topic: What counts as the pilot materials
misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree to 'review the pilot materials' before coding begins.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 believes this includes the intervention manual, message library, and standardized patient call scripts that define the behavior change content.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 believes this includes all artifacts used during delivery, including staff prompts, escalation templates, scheduling instructions, and local onboarding documents.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both routinely use the phrase 'materials' as a catch-all, and in a planning conversation it sounds naturally comprehensive enough that neither feels a need to enumerate every document type.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree that Alex will coordinate 'the training package' for coders and site staff.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means a compact research training set: taxonomy overview, coding rules, two worked examples, and one calibration session for a small coding group.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means a deployment-ready package: slide deck, facilitator guide, attendance tracking, FAQ, and a short competency check that can be reused by multiple sites.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Training package is a familiar planning term that each person encounters in their own context; because both see training as necessary, the phrase creates false consensus without forcing detail.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They align on having the pilot 'ready by July 15' for the consortium check-in.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 thinks readiness means the plan, sampled corpus, codebook draft, and acceptable initial inter-coder agreement are prepared for internal presentation at the check-in.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 thinks readiness means the materials, training assets, and responsibilities are finalized enough that external partner sites can begin immediate execution after the check-in.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: A date milestone feels concrete, so both experience it as clarified already; the hidden difference is not the date itself but the threshold for what qualifies as 'ready,' which often remains implicit.

misalignment_points.topic: Who the international version is for
misalignment_points.surface_form: They discuss making examples usable for 'the international sites.'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 presupposes this refers only to the three established consortium sites whose leads already know the project and can translate local details informally.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 presupposes this refers to a broader downstream audience of operational teams in those countries, requiring examples and workflows to be locally legible from the outset.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both know the project is international and both refer to sites in the same countries, so the category label sounds shared even though one imagines a narrow set of collaborators and the other imagines a wider implementation network.

turns.inner_thought: I need this six-week pilot to look methodologically solid by the consortium check-in without ballooning into a full operations build. For me, ready by July 15 means we have the codebook draft, sampled intervention content, and early agreement figures in shape for internal review. If we can show a credible workflow and initial reliability, that's enough to support a later methods paper and avoid rework.
turns.utterance: Thanks for making time. I thought we could use today to lock the shape of the six-week pilot for applying BCT taxonomy v1 to the medication-adherence program, and make sure we're aligned on what needs to be ready by July 15 for the consortium check-in.

turns.inner_thought: Good. I want this to land as something leadership can see turning into a real rollout asset, not just an academic coding exercise. Ready by July 15 should mean site leads can pick it up and start preparing right away, and the international sites need something practical enough to travel beyond the three people already on consortium calls.
turns.utterance: That works for me. I’d like us to come out with something the international sites can actually use, so if we can map owners and dates today, we’ll be in a much better place for July 15.

turns.inner_thought: First step is straightforward: review the core intervention specification and patient-facing content so the coding frame is anchored in what participants actually receive. I don't need to get pulled into every local implementation artifact before we can start coding.
turns.utterance: From my side, the cleanest starting point is a quick review of the pilot materials so the coding frame is anchored before coding begins.

turns.inner_thought: Yes, and I should make sure that review includes the full delivery set, not just the obvious core documents. If we gather everything a site would touch into one place now, we can reuse that folder later and avoid another scramble when people ask for operational details.
turns.utterance: Agreed. I can pull the pilot materials into one folder for that review so we’re all working from the same set.

turns.inner_thought: I can own the research-facing pieces: coding guide, worked examples, and a compact structure the coders can use. Alex can coordinate the training package once those are drafted, as long as that doesn't turn into my team producing a big reusable onboarding product.
turns.utterance: Great. I can draft the coding guide and an example set, and then you can coordinate the training package once those pieces are ready.

turns.inner_thought: Perfect. I'll shape the training package so site leads can run it consistently later without depending on Nina's team. If we build it once in a reusable way, that helps both the pilot and the broader operational case for the international sites.
turns.utterance: Happy to do that. I’ll make sure the training package works for site leads as well, including something they can run consistently across teams later.

turns.inner_thought: I want at least two coders through an early calibration round so we can demonstrate the taxonomy is being applied consistently. That will give us enough confidence for the check-in even if the full coding run is still in progress.
turns.utterance: One thing I do want early is a calibration exercise with two coders, so we have confidence in the taxonomy application before the check-in and can fold that into the training package.

turns.inner_thought: If July 15 is the readiness date, I need to work backward so the materials, training package, and ownership lines are all settled before then. My assumption is that after the meeting we should be able to hand over a pretty complete pack for sites to start acting on immediately.
turns.utterance: That makes sense. I’ll build the July schedule backward from that point, and I’m assuming we want a fairly complete pack to hand over right after the meeting once the pilot is ready by July 15.

turns.inner_thought: For the international sites, the existing English-language reminder content should be a fine base. The three partner institutions already know the project, so light adaptation in examples is enough; we don't need a full localization exercise before the check-in.
turns.utterance: Yes, and for the examples, I’d like them to be easy for the international sites to follow. We can use the current English-language medication reminder content as the base set.

turns.inner_thought: Using the current content is fine as a starting point, but I should flag wording and workflow differences early if this is going to be legible for broader teams in each country. Better to design with local pathways in mind now than retrofit later.
turns.utterance: Sounds good. I’ll flag a few wording and workflow differences the international sites may want reflected in their local versions, so we’re not surprised later.

turns.inner_thought: So my lane is clear: codebook draft, sample selection from the core intervention content, and coder calibration. If I can get those into shape, then from my perspective the pilot is ready by July 15 for the consortium review.
turns.utterance: So, on my side: I’ll draft the codebook, select the sample from the pilot materials, and set up coder calibration so the pilot is ready by July 15.

turns.inner_thought: And I’ll make sure the wider delivery set is organized, the training package is something sites can actually run, and there’s a clear handoff after July 15 for teams across the international sites. That should show this collaboration is operationally useful, not just analytically interesting.
turns.utterance: And on mine: I’ll organize the pilot materials folder, shape the training package, and prepare a handoff path for the international sites after July 15. That should give us a solid plan going into the consortium check-in.
